tables: Daily snapshot of period H/L/AvgVol per instrument. Computed by period_metrics_compute.py after market close.
Weekly-rebuilt GICS sector benchmark statistics (median / P25 / P75) from screener.universe
Weekly top-5 picks from ASX200 ranked by composite factor score (AlphaFive strategy). pick_month stores the Monday date of each week.

market.daily_metrics: 1 if close > 20-day rolling VWAP, else 0. Simple mean-reversion / momentum signal.
Average daily dollar turnover over 20 days (AUD millions): close × avg_volume_20d / 1,000,000. Primary liquidity risk filter — stocks < $0.5M/day are illiquid.

Calendar three-year price return, anchored on the last close at or before date - 3 years and within the declared grace. NULL where no such close exists or the window spans an unreconciled corporate action; the reason is in metric_states. Replaces market.yearly_metrics.return_3y, which was anchored without a grace bound and ended at the fiscal period end.

Per-metric state for the calendar price windows: metric -> {state, cause, reason, observed}. Sparse -- an entry exists only for a metric whose state is not APPLICABLE, so a populated numeric column must never sit beside an entry, and a NULL numeric column with no entry is a contract violation rather than a default. NULL (not '{}') means the row was never assessed: written before FACTOR_MODEL_V3 or by a producer that does not assess. Same vocabulary as screener.universe.metric_states.
market.sector_benchmarks: Per-metric benchmark state: metric -> {state, reason_code, n_total_peers, n_applicable_peers, n_valid_peers, coverage_pct}. A numeric median column that is NULL with no entry here predates this contract; a NULL with an entry has a stated reason. Applicable benchmarks carry counts too, so the denominator is always visible.

The run that produced this benchmark. Must match the compute_run_id of the screener.universe rows it contextualises: a factor score and the peer statistic shown beside it have to come from the same assessment set and the same model version.
market.yearly_metrics: 3-year rolling average ROIC. Sustained >12-15% = durable competitive advantage.
5-year rolling average ROIC. Better signal for moat quality than single-year ROIC.
Operating cash flow / net profit — earnings quality (cash conversion). >1 = strong.
Dividends paid / free cash flow — FCF-based payout sustainability. <0.75 = sustainable.
3-year CAGR of shares outstanding — positive = dilution, negative = buyback.
Coefficient of variation of EPS over 5 years (std/|mean|). Lower = more stable earnings.
Count of consecutive years (most recent first) with positive free cash flow.
Asset-light composite score 0-3: +1 if capex_intensity<5%, +1 if fcf_margin>10%, +1 if asset_turnover>0.5. Score 3 = highly asset-light (tech/software/services).
Pricing power / moat proxy (0–3): +1 avg_roe_5y>15%, +1 avg_roic_5y>12%, +1 fcf_margin>10%.
Scalability / network-effect proxy (0–3): +1 revenue_cagr_5y>10%, +1 capex_intensity<5%, +1 roic>15%.
Earnings predictability proxy (0–3): +1 eps_volatility_5y<0.20, +1 fcf_positive_years>=4, +1 revenue_cagr_5y>0.
strategy.monthly_picks: Monday of the week for which these picks were computed (e.g. 2026-05-19 = week of 19 May 2026).
TRUE for the current week's picks only. All other weeks are FALSE (kept as history).
